description.narrative: The project will support the Government of Pakistan's national social safety net program, the Benazir Income Support Program (BISP). The project will enable the expansion of the cash transfer program (paid to the female head of targeted poor families) by registering an additional 2.4 million eligible families and financing the first few quarters of their cash transfers. In addition, it will support the strengthening and phased expansion of the pilot health insurance and skills development programs to increase income and good health for targeted families. The project will provide technical support and finance part of the scaling-up costs of both programs using a performance-based allocation. The substantial fiduciary risk of the project will be mitigated through the strengthening of BISP financial management systems and capacity.

Output: Cash transfer program coverage expanded Indicator: 100% of all eligible female heads of families with the CNIC enrolled in BISP (2013 baseline: 70%) (2018 baseline: 95%) Progress/Status: By the end of Dec 2019, approximately 855K beneficiaries have been enrolled under ADB loan out of total 5.4 million eligible beneficiaries receiving the cash transfers. The ADB beneficiaries are 16% of total eligible beneficiaries. Now after updates in the poverty status and enrolment of beneficiaries through new partner banks, a total of 4.5 million beneficiaries remain. The ADB beneficiaries are about 15% of total eligible beneficiaries. In 2019 BISP started cleansing the 10-year-old beneficiaries' database through data analytics and identified 820,165 ineligible beneficiaries in the database, getting benefitted from BISP. Of this, 14,730 were the government officers. All these ineligible beneficiaries (about 15% of the total) were removed from the database.
As of 31 March 2023, 8.96 million eligible beneficiaries are enrolled in the program, which include new beneficiaries identified under the NSER update.
As of 27/07/2023, 9.003 million eligible beneficiaries are enrolled in the program, which include new beneficiaries identified under the NSER update.
As of 27/10/2023, for the FY 2023-24, the cash transfer program has been expanded to have 9.3 million beneficiaries enrolled under UCT Kafaalat program by June 2024.
As of 31 Dec 2023 the target of 9.3 million has been achieved.
$4.5m disbursement to beneficiaries was made in last quarter of 2024.

Output: Financial management and control systems, and policy research improved Indicator: Engendered research conducted in inline with research framework from Q1-2015 onwards (2014 baseline: not applicable) Progress/Status: Delayed. Researcher is not yet hired.
PRU researchers have developed the research plan.
PRU became functional in April 2021. Since its establishment, it has developed a Research Strategy for BISP, which outlines key areas of focus of research and different forms of research output to be produced and disseminated. Under this framework, a number of research activities have been carried out to date with respect to BISP's different programmatic interventions, over the last 2 years. Some of the main activities in this regard include the following: Assessment/ Process Evaluation of Benazir Scholarships for Undergraduates (BSU) Development of a Strategy for implementing Knowledge Management System in BISP Development of Paper on Social Protection for Persons with Disabilities Survey on welfare options for people living in Jhuggis/ slums in Islamabad/ Rawalpindi Collaborative research with UNDP for development of a series of three policy briefs Analysis of Population Dynamics using new NSER data Development of Agile Model for action research Beneficiary Needs Assessment Survey Development of customized Business Intelligence Dashboards for improvement in operations & fraud detection UCT/ CCT Payment Alerts Payment Complaints Management System BI Tool for sharing of NSER data Risk assurance framework Budget variance analysis tools Fake URL blocking analysis
However the gender focus of all the above research work is yet to be evaluated.
June 2025: BISP PRU has so far produced the following studies and research work i) Analysis Report: Appropriate Benefit Level for BISP UCT Beneficiaries; ii) BISP in Focus - Digital Library Document (Vol. I); iii) BISP Methods of Fund Disbursement and International Practices; iv) Cost-Benefit Analysis of BISP Call Center; v) Vocational Training Through Mobile Phones: The Best Alternative for Poverty Alleviation; vi) Graduating UCT Beneficiaries through Manufacturing and Buy-Back Schemes; vii) Comparative Analysis of Beneficiary Identification Methods in Global Poverty Alleviation Programs; viii) Performance Analysis Report NSER Data Entry Executives (DEE)
October 2025: During a recent meeting at the BISP office, it was confirmed that BISP will share the TORs for the two long-pending research studies (i) Operational Review of BISP's Nationwide Nashonuma Program and (ii) Comparative Study of BISP's Payment System, as agreed under the latest procurement plan.
